swap.evidence: Products tried: a GP surgery appointment booker and a library study-room booker. Surviving unchanged: the masthead (name in bold body sans and a small glyph), pale ground with white bordered boxes, outlined day chips, square time-tile grid, filled green 'Next', 'There is a problem' summary, summary card with Change links, reference card. Bound to this product: only copy (Quarry Road, DRC- permit, waste list with limits, 'not on the gate's list') and the bin glyph. With the name and copy hidden, a reader could not tell this is a tip booking.

category_guess.evidence: Predicted default for a UK council transactional service: off-white ground, one sans, bold sentence-case headings, a single green or blue filled button, text step indicator, red-bordered error summary, check-your-answers card, confirmation panel with a reference. Every identity-carrying choice here matches it (ground, sans, green button, error summary, summary card, 'Booked' + reference). Predicted opposite (a branded, illustrated eco look) is also absent, so nothing was chosen against the default either.

similar_prompt.evidence: Brief: 'booking flow for a council leisure centre's swimming-lane slots, mostly on phones'. Predicted: day chips, a grid of 20-30 minute tiles with availability tags, one filled green button, plain form, confirmation with reference. Overlap is near total; nothing in the frame was driven by vehicles, the gate or the yard.

evidence: All three tests fail on the identity-carrying elements: masthead, ground, type voice, slot tiles, done-page reference card.
Specificity lives only in the copy (DRC- permit, 'Rubble (up to four bags)', 'This booking is not on the gate's list'), which is good copy on a portable frame.
Convention in structure is correct for Operate surfaces and is not counted against it; the problem is that no brand layer sits on top.

attributes.x_evidence: Council name in the masthead, phone number and weekday hours in the footer, matter-of-fact copy ('Nothing is paid.', 'Questions: 01632 960771'), no marketing hero, no imagery, sentence case throughout.
One typeface, borders not shadows, rules beside controls, one filled button per step.
attributes.y_evidence: No identity beyond the name in body bold; done page reference not treated as something to show at a gate; empty right half on wide screens; done page ending with an empty grey band; 'Opening days' and 'At the centre' are heading-plus-paragraph boxes. This lands on bare.

attributes.pair: firm about the rules, not stern
attributes.x_evidence: 'Rubble is limited to four bags and mattresses to two', 'Starts DRC-, then five digits.', 'This booking is not on the gate's list.', 'To confirm you live in the district.' Each rule sits next to its control; red kept for errors.
attributes.y_evidence: Error heading 'There is a problem' is standard and neutral; nothing stern seen.

brand_fit.tone: formal-leaning, serious, respectful, matter-of-fact; matches the declared 'gate attendant' voice

mode_fit: All four surfaces are Operate or Read and stay quiet and conventional, which is right; no hero moments, no motion seen. The gap is the identity floor (ADR-035), not too little expression for the mode.

specificity.label: judged
specificity.evidence: Anchor 1: product content (real copy, the DRC- permit, the waste limits) sits on a frame that fails swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests.

hierarchy.label: judged
hierarchy.evidence: Anchor 2: wide views read heading > chips/tiles > Next, and confirm reads clearly; but the slot area splits into an unlabelled 'Few left' group above 'Morning', and in the cancelled done state the heading 'Booked' and the big reference outrank the red cancellation line; in the expired confirm state 'Book this slot' stays the primary.

coherence.label: judged
coherence.evidence: Anchor 3: one type family, one radius, borders-only depth, one green across routes and a composed dark theme; lapse: vehicle chips (black regular) differ from day chips (green bold) for the same control type.

restraint.label: judged
restraint.evidence: Capped at 2: nothing is loud or decorative, but there is no signature or focal point on any screen (DSL-080).

brand_fit.label: judged
brand_fit.evidence: 'civic, not corporate' and 'firm about the rules, not stern' reflected through copy and layout; 'plain, not bare' drifts to bare on every primary surface.

execution.label: judged
execution.evidence: Anchor 2: spacing and alignment clean at 1280; rough at the edges: (i) button stranded on its own line at 375, done page ending with an empty grey band at 1280, half-empty width on vehicle/confirm, duplicate date line on the when screen, '–' placeholder in the expired summary.

appeal.label: judged
appeal.evidence: Matches the 'plain' verdict: clean but bare; identity is the name; no screen has anything to look at.

detector_comparison.post_unseal_notes: Detectors reported nothing; this does not change the verdicts. The absence of tells is consistent with a clean but plain page.

findings.title: Cancelled booking still headed 'Booked' and told to show the reference at the gate
findings.description: On the done page in the cancelled state, the h1 still reads 'Booked', the reference DR-204117 keeps its large bold treatment, and under the red line 'Status: cancelled. This booking is not on the gate's list.' the copy still says 'Show this at the gate, on your phone or on paper' and 'A reminder will be sent to your mobile the evening before.'
findings.impact: The two strongest elements say the opposite of the status line, which is small and sits below them.

harm.statement: A resident opening this page the evening before may read 'Booked' and the big reference, drive a loaded car to Quarry Road and be turned away at the gate because the booking is not on the list.

evidence.detail: heading 'Booked' at y≈118; red status at y≈275; 'Show this at the gate' at y≈301

findings.recommendation: Decide what the cancelled state leads with: the status should own the heading and the reference treatment, and the gate and reminder lines should not appear for a booking that is not on the list.

findings.title: Done page does not restate the day, slot time or vehicle that was booked
findings.description: The done page shows only the reference, generic gate instructions and 'Book another slot'. The day (Saturday 17 October), the slot (09:20 to 09:40), the vehicle and the waste, all present on the confirm page, are absent.
findings.impact: The surface's single job is 'know the booking is made and what to show at the gate'; when to arrive is the scarce thing and is not on the page the resident keeps.

harm.statement: A resident who books in the evening and checks the done page next morning cannot see which 20-minute slot they have, and the gate checks the vehicle against the booking without the page showing which vehicle was booked.

evidence.detail: no date, time or vehicle text anywhere on the page; same at 375-dark

findings.recommendation: Decide what the gate pass consists of (reference, day, slot, vehicle) and give it one composed block the resident can show from the phone.

findings.title: 'Few left' slots are pulled out of time order into an unlabelled group above 'Morning'
findings.description: On the when screen, every slot tagged 'Few left' (e.g. 08:20, 08:40, 09:00, 09:40, 10:20, 10:40, 13:40, 14:00, 15:00, 16:40 on Saturday) sits in a group with no heading above 'Morning'. The 'Morning' and 'Afternoon' groups then show only the remaining times, so 'Morning' jumps 08:00, 09:20, 10:00 and afternoon times appear in two places.
findings.impact: Residents scan by time of day ('Saturday morning'); the grouping breaks the time sequence the labels promise.

harm.statement: A resident looking under 'Morning' for 08:20 or 09:00 may conclude those slots do not exist or are gone and pick a worse time or another day, although they are free in the unlabelled group above.

evidence.detail: ten 'Few left' tiles above the 'Morning' label; Morning row 08:00, 09:20, 10:00, 11:00...

findings.recommendation: Decide whether scarcity or time of day orders the grid; if time of day, keep every slot in its period and let the tag carry 'Few left'.

findings.title: Expired-hold state keeps 'Book this slot' as the only primary and shows a dash for the slot
findings.description: On confirm with hold=expired the error summary says 'This slot is no longer available.' with no link, the summary row reads 'Slot – · Change slot', and the filled 'Book this slot' button remains the only primary at the bottom of a filled-in form.
findings.impact: The recovery action (choose another slot) is a small underlined link inside the card; the strongest element on the page is an action that cannot succeed.

harm.statement: A resident whose held slot expired is likely to press 'Book this slot' again rather than find the small 'Change slot' link, slowing the booking when slots are scarce.

findings.recommendation: Decide what the one filled action is in this state; it should be the recovery, with the error summary linking to it.

findings.title: Permit number field shown before any vehicle is chosen
findings.description: On the vehicle step's default and errors states, with no vehicle selected, the 'Permit number' label, 'Starts DRC-, then five digits.' hint and input are shown directly under the chips, with nothing saying it is only for vans and trailers (that rule is behind the (i) button).
findings.impact: DESIGN.md: 'Do state a rule where it applies.' The field appears where the rule does not apply.

harm.statement: A resident with an ordinary car may think they need a DRC- permit they do not have and stop or call the council, since the 'vans and trailers only' rule is hidden behind the info button.

findings.recommendation: Decide whether the permit field belongs only to the van and trailer choices, or carries its own 'vans and trailers only' line where it sits.

findings.title: No identity layer: the frame is a portable council form
findings.description: Across all four surfaces the only identity is 'Dunmore District Council' in bold body text and a small bin glyph; type, colour, tiles and cards are the category default. The recycling centre, the yard and the gate leave no visual trace; the done-page reference is bold text in a white card.
findings.impact: Design note: 'plain, not bare' asks for an identity floor; the pages read bare.
findings.recommendation: Decide one element from the centre's own world (the gate pass, the site, the waste streams) that carries identity quietly on every step, starting with the done-page reference.

findings.title: Empty bands and half-empty width at desktop widths
findings.description: Vehicle and confirm at 1280 put a ~610px form column on the left with the right half empty; done at 1280 ends at ~715px with the white footer band and an empty grey band below it.
findings.impact: Design note: reads unfinished on desktop, the minority device.
findings.recommendation: Decide how the page ends at short content lengths and what, if anything, the wide right column holds.

findings.title: Vehicle chips and day chips are drawn as two different control styles
findings.description: Day chips on the when screen use green bold labels with green borders; vehicle chips on the next step use black regular labels with grey borders, though both are single-choice segmented controls.
findings.impact: Design note: a small coherence lapse between consecutive steps.
findings.recommendation: Decide one treatment for single-choice chips and use it on both steps.

findings.title: Info button stranded on its own line at 375
findings.description: At 375 the (i) button wraps below 'Car / Car with trailer / Van' and sits alone on a second row, directly above the 'Permit number' label.
findings.impact: Design note: reads as a stray control on the main device.
findings.recommendation: Decide where the permit explanation lives on narrow screens so it stays attached to what it explains.

strengths: Copy states each rule beside its control in the gate attendant's voice ('Rubble is limited to four bags and mattresses to two', 'To confirm you live in the district').
The dark theme is composed, not inverted: lighter green actions, dark surfaces with cards lighter than the ground, amber and grey tags still legible.
One filled button per step, borders-only depth and a single radius hold across all routes.
keep: Keep the plain, rule-beside-the-control voice and the one-filled-button-per-step discipline while adding identity.
